newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa seeks lower airport/air traffic costs.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa seeks lower airport/air traffic costs.

text.p: Air travel liberalisation in Europe must be followed by deregulation of airport and air traffic control charges, Deutsche Lufthansa chairman Juergen Weber said.

EU airlines were adapting to market conditions and cost pressures but airports and air traffic control have not yet been subject to competition, he added in a speech prepared for delivery on Wednesday to the 5th Frankfurt Air Travel Symposium.
Lufthansa had reduced operating unit costs by 2.5 percent a year from 1990-95 but air traffic control and airport fees had risen 4.2 percent a year on average, he said.
Infrastructure users and not taxpayers should bear the costs of services, and Schiphol airport should not be subsidised while Frankfurt airport had to earn all its revenue through fees, Weber said.
"When we have 100 percent cost-covering in German air traffic, it cannot be right that the Dutch taxpayer helps Schiphol airport to a competitive advantage," he said.
Since the third stage of EU air liberalisation in 1987, six percent more routes have been flown, cabotage was offered on 20 EU routes and 20 of 80 new entrants were still operating, he added.
Cabotage allows an airline from one EU country to fly passengers and cargo between two points of another EU country or between two points of two other EU countries.
But the average airline yield fell about 20 percent over the last ten years and the Lufthansa yield per passenger-kilometre- tonne (PKT) fell seven percent from 1991 to 1995, Weber said.

The resulting massive cost pressure has prompted carriers such as British Airways PLc, Lufthansa, SAS and KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV to cost-cutting programmes and new strategic concepts to maintain their competitiveness.
On slots, Weber said only: "The sufficient availability of slots in demand is a decisive factor to ensure the economic status of locations."
But he gave no details of Lufthansa's views on the question of slot liberalisation or possible slot trading.
Lufthansa welcomed moves for the EU to negotiate traffic rights with "large, non-European trading blocks", he added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax+ 5017
